title: Mission: Aurora’s HR assistant
subtitle: Cite the source, refuse when it doesn’t know and hand the delicate stuff to a person
mission: Aurora is opening the HR assistant to all employees. It answers questions from the handbook: it retrieves chunks, cites where the answer came from and, when it doesn’t know or the topic is delicate, it doesn’t improvise. Right now it’s built the worst possible way: the PDF goes in dirty, search only looks at words, only one chunk comes back, there’s no confidence threshold, it doesn’t cite, doesn’t refuse and treats harassment like a benefits question. There are 13 fixed questions: 9 the handbook answers, 2 it doesn’t cover (gym, dog at the office) and 2 delicate ones (harassment and a salary dispute). Fix the setup until all six criteria turn green. (The handbook is the toy one with 12 chunks, and the vector similarities are hand-written; with "In the browser" search uses real vectors.)

coach.ui: Move the controls; the criteria change as you adjust. Each failing one says why, and the table shows what the assistant did with each question.
coach.cmd: Edit the command and run it. Each failing criterion says why. Everything you need showed up in lessons 8 to 15 (clean-up, search, citation and refusal) and 19 (triage).

why.simples:
A good HR clerk does five things without thinking: reads a clean handbook (no repeated pages), looks for the answer by meaning and by exact word, says which page it came from, admits "I don’t know that" and, if the topic is harassment or salary, calls a person instead of answering off the cuff.
You built a clerk like that. Each piece covers the other’s mistake: word-only search doesn’t understand "time off", meaning-only search trips on acronyms like PLR; citation lets you check; refusal prevents invented gym hours; triage hands over what isn’t for a machine.
why.dev:
The pipeline has six stations: clean ingestion (no repeated header, duplicate or hyphen-cut word), hybrid search (BM25 + embeddings, min-max scores mixed with a weight), a top-k that covers compound questions, a confidence gate before the LLM, a prompt with numbered chunks, [n] citation and a fixed refusal sentence, and deterministic triage before anything else.
Triage comes first and doesn’t depend on the model: a trigger list (or a classifier) sends harassment, complaints and salary disputes to a person, with the question and a ticket number. Then comes search; if the best similarity is below the threshold, the code returns the refusal without calling the LLM; otherwise the LLM answers from the chunks only and the code checks that every [n] exists among them. At the end, an evaluation loop runs fixed questions (answerable, outside the handbook, delicate) and measures recall@k, correct answers, correct refusals and correct handoffs, on every change.
why.especialista:
Three traps in this setup. First: the confidence threshold belongs to the embedding model, it isn’t universal. multilingual-e5 cosines sit in a high, narrow band (the model card says that’s expected and that rank matters, not the absolute value), so you calibrate the threshold with real in-scope and out-of-scope questions, and recalibrate when you change the model. In the simulation the working range is narrow on purpose: above it the assistant refuses what the handbook answers, below it, it invents.
Second: triage by trigger list is cheap and predictable, but it errs both ways (a false positive sends "expense claim process" to a person; a false negative lets harassment through without the keyword). In production, combine rules with a classifier, measure the error rate on both sides and prefer erring toward the human on risky topics. Third: 13 questions are a smoke test, not an evaluation set; use tens or hundreds, hold one part out for calibrating and another for measuring, and evaluate faithfulness of the answer to the cited chunk (LLM judge or human), because a valid [n] doesn’t prove the sentence is supported. Log refusals and handoffs: they show what’s missing from the handbook and which topics need a better human flow, and they hold personal data, so decide who may read that log.

success: Mission accomplished! The assistant answered {nCorrect} of the {nAns} handbook questions with an [n] from a chunk that supports them (recall@{k} of {recPct}%), refused the {nOut} the handbook doesn’t cover without refusing any it does (minimum confidence {limitPct}%), handed harassment and salary to a person and indexed a clean handbook. Aurora can open the assistant. What’s left is what no 13-question test shows: real questions, dozens of them, and someone reading the refusal log.

ui: Start with the red criteria: each says why. The table shows what the assistant did with each question.

Look at the confidence column: the threshold sits above the highest confidence of the outside-the-handbook questions and below the lowest of those the handbook answers. And note that search that catches synonyms and acronyms needs words and vectors together, with more than one chunk.
Turn everything on: clean, hybrid search, k 3, threshold 78%, cite, refuse and triage.
cmd: The text goes in quotes; --clean, --cite, --refuse and --triage take yes or no.
--mode takes keyword, vector or hybrid; --k goes from 1 to 6; --threshold goes from 0 to 0.99.
build "hr-assistant" --clean yes --mode hybrid --k 3 --threshold 0.78 --cite yes --refuse yes --triage yes

errors.belowMin.k: At least 1 chunk; with zero the model answers in the dark.
errors.aboveMax.k: Up to 6 chunks: beyond that the context gets expensive and noisy.
errors.belowMin.limit: Confidence can’t be negative. 0 turns the threshold off (and that’s one of the problems).
errors.aboveMax.limit: Up to 0.99: above that no question passes and the assistant refuses everything.

steps:
Create a folder and a Python 3 virtual environment and install the libraries. The first run downloads the embedding model from Hugging Face (a few hundred MB):
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip also installs PyTorch (it can be large). For a smaller, CPU-only install, install it first:
pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
pip install sentence-transformers rank_bm25 anthropic
On Windows, activate with .venv\Scripts\activate. Then keep your Anthropic API key in the environment variable (in PowerShell: $env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = "your-key"):
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="your-key"

Create corpus.py with the handbook (the same 12 chunks as the simulation) and the test questions. Each question carries its kind and the indices (starting at 0) of the chunks that answer it:
CHUNKS = [
    "Vacation must be requested through the employee portal 30 days in advance and needs the manager’s approval.",
    "Vacation can be split into up to three periods: one of at least 14 days and the others of at least 5 days each.",
    "Employees can sell up to one third of their vacation (cash allowance), asking together with the vacation request.",
    "The meal allowance (VR) is R$ 45 per working day; anyone may swap it for the grocery allowance (VA) of the same value.",
    "The health plan covers spouses and children up to 24 as dependents, with co-payment on appointments.",
    "The PLR profit share is paid in March, proportional to how well company and team goals were met the previous year.",
    "Remote work is allowed up to 2 days a week, agreed with the manager at the start of each month.",
    "Anyone with remote days gets a R$ 120 monthly home office allowance, paid with the salary.",
    "Work expenses are reimbursed with an invoice uploaded in the expenses app within 30 days.",
    "Home internet and electricity aren’t reimbursable: those costs are already covered by the home office allowance.",
    "To change your portal password, go to My profile > Security or call IT extension 4000.",
    "To use the VPN, install the corporate app and select the AUR-VPN-02 profile.",
]

# (question, kind, indices of the chunks that answer): "answer" = the handbook answers; "outside" = not in the handbook; "sensitive" = goes to a person
QUESTIONS = [
    ("How far in advance do I request vacation?", "answer", [0]),
    ("Can I split my vacation?", "answer", [1]),
    ("When is the PLR paid?", "answer", [5]),
    ("Which VPN profile do I use?", "answer", [11]),
    ("How long before should I tell them I’ll take time off?", "answer", [0]),
    ("Can I get my home internet bill reimbursed?", "answer", [9, 7]),
    ("What are the company gym’s opening hours?", "outside", []),
    ("My manager is harassing me. What do I do?", "sensitive", []),
]

Create assistant.py. It does triage first (a trigger regex), hybrid search (BM25 with rank_bm25 + multilingual-e5-small embeddings, with the "query: " and "passage: " prefixes that model asks for), refuses by threshold without calling the LLM and, if it passes, asks for the answer with a system prompt that says to cite [n] and use the refusal sentence:
import os, re, unicodedata, uuid
import numpy as np
from anthropic import Anthropic
from rank_bm25 import BM25Okapi
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
from corpus import CHUNKS

K = int(os.environ.get("K", "3"))
LIMIT = float(os.environ.get("LIMIT", "0.80"))
MODEL = os.environ.get("CLAUDE_MODEL", "claude-haiku-5-5")
REFUSAL = "I couldn't find that in the handbook. I'll forward your question to HR."
REFUSAL_MARK = "find that in the handbook"
SYSTEM = (
    "You are Aurora's HR assistant. Answer in English, in one or two sentences, "
    "using only the numbered chunks. End each sentence with the chunk number in brackets, like [3]. "
    f'If the chunks don\'t answer, say exactly: "{REFUSAL}"'
)
SENSITIVE = re.compile(r"harass|discriminat|dispute", re.I)
STOP = {"what", "which", "how", "when", "can", "the", "for", "with", "my", "your", "that", "this", "and", "you", "do", "to", "of", "in", "is", "an", "on", "a", "i", "it", "me", "should", "tell", "them"}

def tokens(text):
    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFD", text.lower())
    text = "".join(c for c in text if unicodedata.category(c) != "Mn")
    return [t for t in re.split(r"[^a-z0-9]+", text) if len(t) > 1 and t not in STOP]

def minmax(x):
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    span = x.max() - x.min()
    return (x - x.min()) / span if span else np.zeros_like(x)

embedder = SentenceTransformer("intfloat/multilingual-e5-small")
vectors = embedder.encode(["passage: " + c for c in CHUNKS], normalize_embeddings=True)
bm25 = BM25Okapi([tokens(c) for c in CHUNKS])
client = Anthropic()

def search(question):
    q = embedder.encode("query: " + question, normalize_embeddings=True)
    sims = vectors @ q
    mix = 0.5 * minmax(sims) + 0.5 * minmax(bm25.get_scores(tokens(question)))
    top = [int(i) for i in np.argsort(-mix)[:K]]
    return top, float(sims.max())

def handle(question):
    if SENSITIVE.search(question):
        text = "I passed your question to a person in HR (ticket HR-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:6] + ")."
        return {"action": "handoff", "text": text, "top": [], "cited": [], "conf": 0.0}
    top, conf = search(question)
    if conf < LIMIT:
        return {"action": "refuse", "text": REFUSAL, "top": top, "cited": [], "conf": conf}
    context = "\n".join(f"[{i + 1}] {CHUNKS[i]}" for i in top)
    reply = client.messages.create(
        model=MODEL,
        max_tokens=300,
        system=SYSTEM,
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": context + "\n\nQuestion: " + question}],
    )
    text = "".join(b.text for b in reply.content if b.type == "text").strip()
    cited = [n - 1 for n in map(int, re.findall(r"\[(\d+)\]", text)) if n - 1 in top]
    action = "refuse" if REFUSAL_MARK in text else "answer"
    return {"action": action, "text": text, "top": top, "cited": cited, "conf": conf}

Create run_eval.py, the evaluation loop: it runs each question and checks search (are the right chunks among the K sent?), citation (does [n] point at a right chunk?), refusal and handoff, then prints a summary. Run it with python run_eval.py:
from assistant import handle, K
from corpus import QUESTIONS

score = {"answer": [0, 0], "outside": [0, 0], "sensitive": [0, 0]}
recalls = []
for question, kind, gold in QUESTIONS:
    r = handle(question)
    if kind == "answer":
        recall = len(set(gold) & set(r["top"])) / len(gold)
        recalls.append(recall)
        ok = r["action"] == "answer" and recall == 1 and bool(set(r["cited"]) & set(gold))
    elif kind == "outside":
        ok = r["action"] == "refuse"
    else:
        ok = r["action"] == "handoff"
    score[kind][0] += ok
    score[kind][1] += 1
    print(("OK " if ok else "XX ") + f"{kind:9} conf={r['conf']:.2f} top={r['top']} | {question}")

mean_recall = sum(recalls) / len(recalls)
print(f"\nrecall@{K}: {mean_recall:.0%} | answers: {score['answer'][0]}/{score['answer'][1]}"
      f" | refusals: {score['outside'][0]}/{score['outside'][1]} | handoffs: {score['sensitive'][0]}/{score['sensitive'][1]}")
print("PASSED" if mean_recall >= 0.8 and all(a == b for a, b in score.values()) else "FAILED")

Calibrate the threshold. Look at the confidence (conf=) printed on the "outside" and the "answer" lines. e5 cosines sit in a narrow band, so the right value is yours: set LIMIT between the highest confidence among the outside-the-handbook questions and the lowest among the answered ones, and run again, for example (in PowerShell: $env:LIMIT = "0.84"; python run_eval.py):
LIMIT=0.84 python run_eval.py
If a question the handbook answers turns into "refuse", lower LIMIT; if the outside question gets answered, raise it. With a single outside question in the test, add a few more to QUESTIONS before trusting the number.

Break it on purpose, as in the mission: with K=1 the compound expense question (two chunks) is no longer fully covered, and without the citation or refusal sentence in SYSTEM the loop shows XX:
K=1 python run_eval.py
recipe.ok: run_eval.py prints one OK or XX line for each of the 8 questions and ends with the summary (recall, answers, refusals and handoffs) and the word PASSED once you have calibrated LIMIT; with K=1 the expense question turns XX.
